analysis:
The only change in this PR is a one-line documentation edit to docs/provider/cli-reference.md at line 2183 (base and head). It extends the `[backend] enabled_models` description: when set, it also bounds coordinator model commands and rollouts, with a link to the operator filter in configuration.md. I read the base text (lines 2135-2519) and head text (lines 1-385). Nothing is executable, no config schema, defaults or code paths change, and no keys, endpoints or trust-boundary behavior are altered.

The edit describes a restrictive control: an operator-side allowlist that narrows what the coordinator can load or roll out. That is consistent with TB-002 (coordinator-to-provider WebSocket), where the provider remains able to constrain coordinator commands, and with A-004 / T-027 / T-012 on model-weight and model-substitution concerns. It does not weaken any mitigation.

The actual enforcement lives in provider code and configuration.md, which are not in this batch. Whether `enabled_models` really bounds coordinator load commands and rollouts is a contract I could not verify from the supplied evidence. If the implementation does not enforce this, the documentation would overstate a control. That would be a documentation-accuracy concern, not a demonstrated regression, and the PR evidence does not show a code change.

The threat-model entries I checked (T-041 prefix cache, TB-002 and related) are unaffected. No threat-model update is needed. The remaining unchanged text in the file (lines 2135-2519 and 1-385) is pre-existing and was not re-reviewed beyond orientation.
